system_description.narrative_title: Europe's struggle to coordinate diplomacy, security and tech support over Ukraine
system_description.narrative_summary: European governments are locked in a contested process of who speaks for Europe and how to engage with Russia over Ukraine—while the US advances its own proposals and critical technologies (Starlink) introduce new leverage points. The system is defined by diplomatic positioning, security guarantees, military and funding flows, and information/technology controls that together shape negotiation space and battlefield resilience.
system_description.scope: European diplomatic and security decision-making related to the Russia–Ukraine war: EU states, NATO members in Europe, Ukraine, Russia, the US, defense-industrial cooperation, military aid and funding decisions, and information/communications controls (e.g., Starlink) that affect operations.
system_description.super_system: The global security order (post-Cold-War Euro-Atlantic architecture and great-power competition)
adjacent_subsystems: Russian domestic politics and security apparatus
Ukrainian military operations and critical infrastructure resilience

variables.name: Collective diplomatic cohesion
variables.description: Degree to which the relevant diplomatic actors present consistent, unified positions and coordinated diplomatic messaging.

variables.name: Negotiation leadership centrality
variables.description: Extent to which authority and initiative for peace negotiations are concentrated in a single actor or subgroup versus dispersed across multiple actors.

variables.name: Military assistance flow rate
variables.description: Rate at which military resources (equipment, munitions, training, and personnel support) are committed and delivered to frontline actors.

variables.name: Defense industrial integration
variables.description: Degree of technical, production and procurement interoperability and cooperation across defense industrial bases.

variables.name: Committed funding stock
variables.description: Cumulative amount of financial resources formally committed to security, military, and reconstruction efforts.

variables.name: Security guarantee strength
variables.description: Perceived firmness and reliability of formal and informal security assurances available to threatened parties.

variables.name: Technological-control leverage
variables.description: Degree to which control over critical technologies and services (communications, ISR, satellites, etc.) can be used to influence operational or diplomatic outcomes.

variables.name: Access to external communications services
variables.description: Availability and reliability of external commercial and third‑party communications and data services supporting operations and coordination.

variables.name: Command-and-control resilience
variables.description: Ability of forces and political actors to maintain command, control, communications and coordination under disruption.

variables.name: Information influence intensity
variables.description: Rate and scale at which narrative framing, propaganda, disinformation, and information operations are produced and disseminated to affect perceptions and behavior.

variables.name: Economic sanction pressure
variables.description: Intensity and breadth of economic restrictions and financial measures applied to coerce or punish target actors.

variables.name: Domestic political support
variables.description: Level of political backing within key constituencies and governments for continued engagement, aid, or negotiation strategies.

variables.name: Inter-party trust
variables.description: Degree of mutual trust and belief in reliability among allied or partnering actors involved in coordination and burden‑sharing.

variables.name: Decision-making tempo
variables.description: Speed at which political and military decisions are formulated, authorized, and implemented across the actor network.

variables.name: Civil infrastructure resilience
variables.description: Robustness and recoverability of critical civil infrastructure (energy, power, transport) that underpin operations and civilian stability.

variables.name: Mediator influence level
variables.description: Ability of neutral or third-party mediators to shape negotiation agendas, access, and acceptable terms across conflicting parties.

catalysts.title: EU five-nation group to represent Europe at peace talks
catalysts.description: Formation and deployment of the EU five-nation delegation to speak for Europe at Ukraine peace negotiations, shaping Europe's negotiating posture and coordination.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'EU settles on five-nation group to speak for Europe at Ukraine peace talks' — centralises European representation, affecting cohesion and mediation.

catalysts.title: Germany's ultimatum over Ukraine funding
catalysts.description: German conditionality and deadline for further Ukraine funding that may accelerate or suspend EU/European financial commitments.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Germany issues ultimatum to secure Ukraine funding' — implies conditional cuts or delays to committed funds and political friction.

catalysts.title: Ongoing Starlink/SpaceX restrictions and outages
catalysts.description: Repeated restrictions and technical disruptions to Starlink/Starshield services and corporate controls, affecting Ukraine's connectivity and defense systems.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Ukraine Says Its Military Starlink Is Disrupted Again', 'Zelenskiy escalates criticism of SpaceX', 'Zelenskiy says restrictions still in place on Starshield'.

catalysts.title: US proposal linking NATO membership to Donbas withdrawal
catalysts.description: Diplomatic push floated by US tying prospective NATO accession/security arrangements to territorial concessions around Donbas, shaping negotiation dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'US floats Nato membership for Donbas withdrawal deal', 'US floated idea of Ukraine ceding Donbas for NATO membership' — shifts negotiation leverage and divides allies.

catalysts.title: US congressional preservation order and likely oversight
catalysts.description: Democratic senators' order for Elon Musk to preserve records on Starlink access may trigger oversight, audits or hearings affecting corporate controls.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Democratic US senators order Musk to preserve records on Ukraine Starlink access', 'Exclusive | Democrats Order Musk to Preserve Records...'.

catalysts.title: Romania offers to fund US troops
catalysts.description: Romania's offer to pay for US soldiers could accelerate US presence and regional burden-sharing arrangements in Eastern Europe.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Romania offers to pay for US soldiers' — may change regional guarantees and burden-sharing quickly.

catalysts.title: Elections in pro‑Russian Moldovan region
catalysts.description: Elections in a restive pro‑Russian Moldovan region may shift regional alignments and Russian influence near EU/NATO borders.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Restive pro-Russian Moldovan region holds elections' — may increase Russian influence and complicate EU/Russia responses.

catalysts.title: Dispute over Germany joining next‑gen fighter project
catalysts.description: Ongoing disagreement between Italy and Germany over entry into a next-generation fighter project, affecting defense industrial cooperation.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Italy says it backs Germany joining next‑generation fighter jet project' and 'Italy rebuffs German bid to enter joint fighter jet project' — signals procurement friction.

catalysts.title: Europe's decision whether to name an envoy to Moscow
catalysts.description: Europe may choose a single envoy or delegation to engage with Moscow for peace talks, testing unity and strategy on engagement with Russia.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Europe dithers over who and how to talk to Putin amid US and Ukraine pressure', 'Moscow tells Europe to pick an envoy...'.
